questions.title: Reversal of non-depolarising blockade by encapsulation
questions.question: Which of the following reverses a non-depolarising neuromuscular blocker by forming a complex with it that diffuses away from the neuromuscular junction into the circulation and is excreted in the urine?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Edrophonium is a short-acting anticholinesterase; it reverses blockade indirectly by raising acetylcholine, not by binding the blocker.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Neostigmine also acts as an anticholinesterase, increasing junctional acetylcholine rather than encapsulating the drug.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Pyridostigmine is likewise an anticholinesterase and does not form a complex with the blocker.
explanations.D: Correct. Sugammadex is a modified gamma-cyclodextrin that directly ENCAPSULATES steroidal non-depolarising blockers (rocuronium, vecuronium) in a tight 1:1 complex. The complex diffuses away from the neuromuscular junction into the plasma and is excreted unchanged in the urine, rapidly ending the block without relying on acetylcholinesterase inhibition. This encapsulation mechanism is unique among the options.

questions.learning_objective: Identify sugammadex as reversing steroidal non-depolarising blockade by direct encapsulation and renal excretion.

questions.title: Autonomic receptor mismatched with its response
questions.question: Each of the following types of receptor is correctly matched with the RESPONSE resulting from its stimulation EXCEPT:

options.B: Alpha-2 adrenergic receptors — increase release of noradrenaline
options.C: Alpha-1 adrenergic receptors — increase blood pressure

explanations.A: Correct match (so not the answer). Muscarinic (M2) stimulation at the SA node slows the heart rate.
explanations.B: Correct answer. This is the WRONG match: presynaptic alpha-2 adrenoceptors mediate NEGATIVE feedback, so their stimulation DECREASES, not increases, noradrenaline release from the nerve terminal. This autoinhibition is exploited by alpha-2 agonists such as clonidine to lower sympathetic outflow. Because the stated response is the opposite of the true one, this pairing is the exception.
explanations.C: Correct match (so not the answer). Alpha-1 stimulation causes vasoconstriction and raises blood pressure.
explanations.D: Correct match (so not the answer). Beta-2 stimulation relaxes bronchial smooth muscle, causing bronchodilatation.

questions.learning_objective: State that presynaptic alpha-2 adrenoceptors decrease noradrenaline release (autoinhibition).

questions.title: Parasympathomimetic mismatched with its use (parathion)
questions.question: Each parasympathomimetic is paired with an appropriate THERAPEUTIC USE EXCEPT:

explanations.A: Correct pairing (so not the answer). Physostigmine, a lipid-soluble anticholinesterase, is used topically to lower intraocular pressure in glaucoma.
explanations.B: Correct pairing (so not the answer). Neostigmine stimulates the bladder and is used for postoperative urinary retention.
explanations.C: Correct pairing (so not the answer). Short-acting edrophonium is used in the diagnostic (Tensilon) test for myasthenia gravis.
explanations.D: Correct answer. This is the WRONG pairing: parathion is an organophosphate INSECTICIDE, i.e. a CAUSE of anticholinesterase poisoning, not a treatment for it. Organophosphate poisoning is treated with atropine and pralidoxime. Listing parathion as a therapy for the very poisoning it causes makes this the exception.

questions.learning_objective: Recognise parathion as an organophosphate insecticide (a poison), not a treatment for organophosphate poisoning.

questions.title: Why neostigmine is preferred over physostigmine in myasthenia
questions.question: Neostigmine is preferred over physostigmine for treating myasthenia gravis because:

options.B: It has a longer duration of action
options.C: It has an additional direct agonistic action on nicotinic receptors at the muscle end-plate

explanations.A: Incorrect. Both are absorbed; oral absorption is not the distinguishing advantage in myasthenia gravis.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Duration is not the key reason; several anticholinesterases are used, and pyridostigmine actually offers longer action.
explanations.C: Correct. Besides inhibiting acetylcholinesterase, neostigmine has an ADDITIONAL direct agonist action on nicotinic receptors at the skeletal-muscle end-plate. This directly augments neuromuscular transmission where it is needed in myasthenia gravis, giving it an advantage over physostigmine, which lacks this direct end-plate action. That dual mechanism is why it is preferred.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Physostigmine, not neostigmine, crosses the blood-brain barrier; CNS penetration would be a disadvantage in treating a peripheral neuromuscular disease.

questions.learning_objective: Explain that neostigmine's additional direct nicotinic action at the muscle end-plate favours it in myasthenia gravis.

questions.title: Atropine substitute used in Parkinsonism
questions.question: The following atropine substitute is useful in the treatment of Parkinsonism:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Pirenzepine is a selective M1 antagonist used to reduce gastric acid secretion, not a central antiparkinsonian agent.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Hyoscine is used for motion sickness and as a sedative antimuscarinic, not for Parkinsonism.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Homatropine is a topical mydriatic/cycloplegic for the eye.
explanations.D: Correct. Benztropine is a centrally acting antimuscarinic that reduces the relative cholinergic overactivity in the basal ganglia caused by dopamine deficiency, so it relieves the tremor and rigidity of Parkinsonism (especially drug-induced parkinsonism). Its central antimuscarinic action is what makes it the useful atropine substitute here.

questions.learning_objective: Identify benztropine as the centrally acting antimuscarinic used in Parkinsonism.

questions.title: Component NOT part of organophosphate poisoning treatment
questions.question: Treatment of acute organophosphorus poisoning includes all the following EXCEPT:

explanations.A: Incorrect (it IS part of treatment). Pralidoxime reactivates cholinesterase and is a mainstay of therapy.
explanations.B: Correct answer. Methacholine is a direct cholinergic (muscarinic) AGONIST, so giving it would ADD to the acetylcholine excess and worsen the cholinergic crisis; it is therefore NOT part of treatment and is the exception. The genuine measures are atropine, pralidoxime, supportive care and decontamination.
explanations.C: Incorrect (it IS part of treatment). Diazepam controls organophosphate-induced seizures and agitation.
explanations.D: Incorrect (it IS part of treatment). Gastric lavage/decontamination limits further absorption after ingestion.

questions.learning_objective: List the components of organophosphate poisoning management and recognise that a cholinergic agonist (methacholine) is not among them.

questions.title: Endpoint NOT targeted by atropine in organophosphate poisoning
questions.question: The following are target endpoints for atropine therapy in organophosphate poisoning EXCEPT:

explanations.A: Correct answer. Atropinisation aims to REVERSE the cholinergic excess, so a persisting bradycardia below 60/min is a sign of UNDER-treatment, not a therapeutic endpoint. Wanting bradycardia as a goal is the opposite of the aim, making this the exception.
explanations.B: Incorrect (it IS an endpoint). Drying of secretions, shown by dry axillae, is a classic marker of adequate atropinisation.
explanations.C: Incorrect (it IS an endpoint). Mydriasis reflects successful antimuscarinic effect.
explanations.D: Incorrect (it IS an endpoint). Restoring an adequate systolic blood pressure (>80 mmHg) confirms reversal of the cardiovascular depression.

questions.learning_objective: Recognise adequate atropinisation endpoints (dry axillae, mydriasis, adequate blood pressure, reversal of bradycardia).

questions.title: Pharmacological effect NOT produced by atropine
questions.question: Atropine has the following pharmacological effects EXCEPT:

explanations.A: Incorrect (it IS an effect). By blocking muscarinic receptors atropine reduces gastric acid and other secretions.
explanations.B: Incorrect (it IS an effect). Atropine blocks the sphincter pupillae, causing mydriasis.
explanations.C: Correct answer. Atropine is an antimuscarinic, so it relaxes bronchial smooth muscle and causes bronchoDILATION; it does NOT produce bronchoconstriction. The stated effect is the reverse of the truth, making it the exception.
explanations.D: Incorrect (it IS an effect). By blocking vagal M2 tone at the SA node, atropine increases the heart rate.

questions.learning_objective: List atropine's antimuscarinic effects (reduced secretions, mydriasis, tachycardia, bronchodilation) and exclude bronchoconstriction.
